title: Attribution is reported as correlation, not as proven incremental revenue
risk: An attributed revenue figure is presented as revenue the AI created, so the pilot claims causal impact that was never tested and budget is committed on a correlation.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
kpi_dataset.attribution holds W-shaped weights (30/30/30/10) for a single confirmed order of 1000 TWD, and no controlled experiment exists in this repository.
The report is required to state that attribution is a model unless a valid controlled comparison exists.

steps.action: Apply the W-shaped weights to the confirmed order
steps.expected: The 1000 TWD order is split 300/300/100/300 across the four touchpoints and the weights sum to exactly 1.0 with no residual.

steps.action: Aggregate attributed revenue per agent for the window
steps.expected: Each agent's attributed share is reported as its weighted portion, and the sum of all shares equals the attributed order value.

steps.action: Attempt to publish the attributed figure as incremental revenue created by the AI
steps.expected: Publication is refused while no controlled experiment exists; the report labels the figure as attributed correlation.

steps.action: Attempt a variant where one agent alone is credited with the whole order
steps.expected: The single-agent rule applies only when exactly one agent participated; with four touchpoints the 100% claim is rejected.

assertions: Attribution weights sum to 1.0 per order and the per-agent shares sum back to the attributed order value.
No attributed figure is published or labelled as incremental, causal or AI-created revenue before a valid controlled comparison exists.
A single-agent 100% credit applies only when the journey has one touchpoint; multi-touch journeys keep the declared weight model.
The report states the attribution model, the touchpoints used and the absence of an experiment, so a reader cannot mistake correlation for causation.
forbidden: Crediting the full order to one agent to simplify the report.
Presenting a post-hoc comparison of strong and weak days as a controlled experiment.
evidence: Per-order attribution table with the weights and the touchpoints.
Per-agent attributed revenue report with the model statement.
Refusal record for the causal publication attempt.
cleanup: Delete gov- attribution and publication rows after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
prerequisites: No controlled experiment exists and the KPI baseline is not locked, so no causal or incremental revenue claim can be made from this dataset.
